claims.quote: Such a privacy of advertisement will never work, I think, on a large scale; it is probably at or near its maximum development now,
claims.description: Newspapers owned by large advertisers to carry only their own advertising will not succeed on a large scale.

claims.quote: this anticipation of the advertiser-owned paper, like that of hourly papers, and that wonderfully powerful cosmic newspaper syndicate, is simply another instance of prophesying based only on a present trend, an expansion of the obvious, instead of an analysis of determining forces.
claims.description: Hourly newspapers and a single all-powerful world newspaper syndicate are dismissed as unlikely.

claims.quote: Democratic armies and navies are always short, and probably will always be short, of ammunition, paint, training and reserve stores;
claims.description: Democratic governments will keep underfunding the real readiness of their armed forces while inflating nominal units.

claims.quote: In warfare, as I have already indicated, this takes the form of the progressive supersession of the horse and the private soldier—which were the living and sole engines of the old time—by machines,
claims.description: Horses and mass infantry will be progressively replaced by machines in warfare.

claims.quote: The new war will probably have none of these features of the old system of fighting.
claims.description: Future war will lose massed charges, decisive set-piece battles and cavalry pursuits.

claims.quote: One can conceive it provided in the future with cross-thread telescopic sights, the focussing of which, corrected by some ingenious use of hygroscopic material, might even find the range, and so enable it to be used with assurance up to a mile or more.
claims.description: Rifles with crosshair telescopic sights that also find the range, accurate out to a mile.

claims.quote: It will be used either for single shots or to quiver and send a spray of almost simultaneous bullets out of a magazine evenly and certainly, over any small area the rifleman thinks advisable.
claims.description: A selective-fire automatic rifle that can fire single shots or bursts like a machine gun.

claims.quote: It will, just as probably, be slung with its ammunition and equipment upon bicycle wheels, and be the common care of two or more associated soldiers.
claims.description: A wheeled rifle served by a team of two or more soldiers.

claims.quote: Save for their liability to such attacks, a few hundreds of such men could hold positions of a quite vast extent, and a few thousand might hold a frontier.
claims.description: Small teams of concealed marksmen will be able to hold vast defensive positions, even a whole frontier.

claims.quote: If the ground they occupied were to be properly tunnelled and trenched, even that might not avail, and there would be nothing for it but to attack them by an advance under cover either of the night or of darkness caused by smoke-shells, or by the burning of cover about their position.
claims.description: Tunnelled and trenched positions attacked only under night or smoke-shell screens.

claims.quote: this will be the opening phase of the struggle, a vast duel all along the frontier between groups of skilled marksmen, continually being relieved and refreshed from the rear.
claims.description: Wars between neighboring nations will open with a continuous front of entrenched marksmen along the whole frontier.

claims.quote: But somewhere far in the rear the central organizer will sit at the telephonic centre of his vast front, and he will strengthen here and feed there and watch, watch perpetually the pressure, the incessant remorseless pressure that is seeking to wear down his countervailing thrust.
claims.description: Commanders will direct a vast front from a rear headquarters linked by telephone instead of leading in the field.

claims.quote: Behind the thin firing line that is actually engaged, the country for many miles will be rapidly cleared and devoted to the business of war, big machines will be at work making second, third, and fourth lines of trenches that may be needed if presently the firing line is forced back,
claims.description: Machines digging multiple reserve lines of trenches behind the front.

claims.quote: there will be a vast and rapid shifting to and fro of big and very long range guns.
claims.description: Very long-range heavy guns rapidly moved along motor roads behind the front.

claims.quote: These guns will probably be fought with the help of balloons.
claims.description: Observation balloons used all along the front to direct long-range artillery fire.

claims.quote: For eight miles on either side of the firing lines—whose fire will probably never altogether die away while the war lasts—men will live and eat and sleep under the imminence of unanticipated death
claims.description: Continuous front lines where firing never stops and soldiers live for long periods under constant threat of death.

claims.quote: Such will be the opening phase of the war that is speedily to come.
claims.description: A great war of this new kind is coming soon.

claims.quote: The battalion commander will be replaced in effect by the organizer of the balloons and guns by which his few hundreds of splendid individuals will be guided and reinforced.
claims.description: Small independent units of skilled soldiers replace massed battalions, coordinated by staff organizing observation and artillery.

claims.quote: a practical realization of socialistic conceptions will quite inevitably be forced upon the fighting State.
claims.description: Total war forces the state to take over industry, transport and supply, in effect a socialist organization.

claims.quote: the dealers in food and clothing, the manufacturers of all sorts of necessary stuff, will be converted by the mere declaration of war into public servants;
claims.description: On the declaration of war all food, clothing and manufacturing businesses become arms of the state.

claims.quote: The organized staffs of the big road managements, now become a part of the military scheme, will be deporting women and children and feeble people and bringing up supplies and supports;
claims.description: Organized mass evacuation of women, children and the weak from war zones.

claims.quote: I imagine that in this ideal war as compared with the war of to-day, there will be a very considerable restriction of the rights of the non-combatant.
claims.description: The legal distinction protecting non-combatants will erode as whole nations are organized for war.

claims.quote: In our imaginary twentieth century State, organized primarily for war, this tendency to differentiate a non-combatant mass in the fighting State will certainly not be respected, the State will be organized as a whole to fight as a whole, it will have triumphantly asserted the universal duty of its citizens.
claims.description: Total war in which the entire population and economy of the state is mobilized.

claims.quote: As the bells ring and the recording telephones click into every house the news that war has come,
claims.description: News broadcast instantly into every home by recording telephones.

claims.quote: no bawling upon the moving platforms of the central urban nuclei,
claims.description: Moving walkways as standard transport in city centers.

claims.quote: Recruiting among the working classes—or, more properly speaking, among the People of the Abyss—will have dwindled to the vanishing point;
claims.description: Armies will stop recruiting the unskilled poor and depend on educated, able men.

claims.quote: In the warfare that will go on in the highly-organized European States of the opening century, the special military balloon used in conjunction with guns, conceivably of small calibre but of enormous length and range, will play a part of quite primary importance.
claims.description: Military balloons spotting for very long-range guns will be central to European war in the new century.

claims.quote: These guns will be carried on vast mechanical carriages, possibly with wheels of such a size as will enable them to traverse almost all sorts of ground.
claims.description: Self-propelled artillery on huge mechanical carriages able to cross almost any terrain.

claims.quote: The aeronauts, provided with large scale maps of the hostile country, will mark down to the gunners below the precise point upon which to direct their fire, and over hill and dale the shell will fly—ten miles it may be—to its billet, camp, massing night attack, or advancing gun.
claims.description: Aerial observers using maps to direct indirect artillery fire onto unseen targets up to ten miles away.

claims.quote: Great multitudes of balloons will be the Argus eyes of the entire military organism, stalked eyes with a telephonic nerve in each stalk, and at night they will sweep the country with search-lights and come soaring before the wind with hanging flares.
claims.description: Large fleets of telephone-linked observation balloons with searchlights and flares for constant surveillance.

claims.quote: Certainly they will be steerable.
claims.description: Military balloons will be steerable dirigibles.

claims.quote: I am inclined to think that the many considerations against a successful attack on balloons from the ground, will enormously stimulate enterprise and invention in the direction of dirigible aerial devices that can fight.
claims.description: The difficulty of shooting down balloons from the ground will spur the invention of fighting aircraft.

claims.quote: Few people, I fancy, who know the work of Langley, Lilienthal, Pilcher, Maxim, and Chanute, but will be inclined to believe that long before the year a.d. 2000, and very probably before 1950, a successful aeroplane will have soared and come home safe and sound.
claims.description: A successful powered aeroplane flight will happen well before 2000 and probably before 1950.
claims.stated_time: long before the year a.d. 2000, and very probably before 1950

claims.quote: Directly that is accomplished the new invention will be most assuredly applied to war.
claims.description: The aeroplane will be put to military use as soon as it is invented.

claims.quote: I am inclined to think the practicable navigable balloon will be first attained by the use of a device already employed by Nature in the swimming-bladder of fishes.
claims.description: A navigable airship using contractible gas bags, modeled on a fish's swim bladder, to rise and fall at will.

claims.quote: A row of such contractile balloons, hung over a long car which was horizontally expanded into wings, would not only allow that car to rise and fall at will, but if the balloon at one end were contracted and that at the other end expanded,
claims.description: A winged airship that steers and glides by contracting gas bags at one end and expanding them at the other.

claims.quote: From some such crude beginning a form like a soaring, elongated, flat-brimmed hat might grow, and the possibilities of adding an engine-driven screw are obvious enough.
claims.description: Flying craft developing into a flat-winged shape driven by an engine-powered propeller.

claims.quote: It would probably have at most a small machine-gun or so, which might fire an explosive shell at the balloons of the enemy, or kill their aeronauts with distributed bullets.
claims.description: Aircraft armed with machine guns to attack enemy balloons and their crews.

claims.quote: The thing would be a sort of air-shark, and one may even venture to picture something of the struggle the deadlocked marksmen of 1950, lying warily in their rifle-pits, will see.
claims.description: By 1950 entrenched, deadlocked soldiers will watch air combat overhead.

claims.quote: I incline to imagine there will be a steel prow with a cutting edge at either end of the sort of aerostat I foresee, and conceivably this aerial ram will be the most important weapon of the affair.
claims.description: Fighting airships fitted with steel cutting prows to ram enemy balloons.

claims.quote: Quite certainly those flying machines will carry folded parachutes, and the last phase of many a struggle will be the desperate leap of the aeronauts with these in hand, to snatch one last chance of life out of a mass of crumpling, fallen wreckage.
claims.description: Military aircrews carrying folded parachutes to bail out of wrecked aircraft.

claims.quote: But in such a fight between flying-machine and flying-machine as we are trying to picture, it will be a fight of hawks, complicated by bullets and little shells.
claims.description: Aerial dogfights between armed flying machines.

claims.quote: They will rush up and up to get the pitch of one another, until the aeronauts sob and sicken in the rarefied air, and the blood comes to eyes and nails.
claims.description: Air combat at altitudes high enough to cause altitude sickness in pilots.

claims.quote: The mere ascent of one flying-ram from one side will assuredly slip the leashes of two on the other, until the manœuvring squadrons may be as thick as starlings in October.
claims.description: Massed squadrons of fighting aircraft in large air battles.

claims.quote: Once the command of the air is obtained by one of the contending armies, the war must become a conflict between a seeing host and one that is blind.
claims.description: Air superiority will become decisive, leaving the side that loses it blind.

claims.quote: Everybody everywhere will be perpetually and constantly looking up, with a sense of loss and insecurity,
claims.description: Enemy control of the air will create widespread fear among the losing country's whole population.

claims.quote: By day the victor's aeroplanes will sweep down upon the apparatus of all sorts in the adversary's rear, and will drop explosives and incendiary matters upon them
claims.description: Aerial bombing with explosives and incendiaries of targets behind enemy lines.

claims.quote: At night his high floating search-lights will go to and fro and discover and check every desperate attempt to relieve or feed the exhausted marksmen of the fighting line.
claims.description: Airborne searchlights used to stop night resupply of the front line.

claims.quote: A general advance will occur under the aerial van, ironclad road fighting-machines may perhaps play a considerable part in this,
claims.description: Armored fighting vehicles taking part in ground offensives under air cover.

claims.quote: Under the moonlight and the watching balloons there will be swift noiseless rushes of cycles, precipitate dismounts, and the never-to-be-quite-abandoned bayonet will play its part.
claims.description: Night assaults by bicycle-mounted infantry.

claims.quote: It will probably be brought about in a civilized country by the seizure of the vital apparatus of the urban regions—the water supply, the generating stations for electricity (which will supply all the heat and warmth of the land), and the chief ways used in food distribution.
claims.description: Conquest will come by seizing cities' water, electricity and food-distribution infrastructure, with electricity supplying all heating.

claims.quote: the generating stations for electricity (which will supply all the heat and warmth of the land)
claims.description: Electricity from generating stations will supply all of a country's heating.

claims.quote: With the destruction of its military apparatus and the prospective loss of its water and food supply, however, the defeated civilized State will probably be willing to seek terms as a whole, and bring the war to a formal close.
claims.description: Defeated states will surrender as a whole once their infrastructure is threatened.

claims.quote: I seem to see a light type of ironclad, armoured thickly only over its engines and magazines, murderously equipped, and with a ram—as alert and deadly as a striking snake.
claims.description: Fast, lightly armored warships with heavy armor only over engines and magazines.

claims.quote: What type of ship may chance to be prevalent when the great naval war comes is hard guessing, but I incline to think that the naval architects of the ablest peoples will concentrate more and more upon speed and upon range and penetration, and, above all, upon precision of fire.
claims.description: Warship design will put speed, gun range, penetration and above all accuracy of fire first.
claims.stated_time: when the great naval war comes

claims.quote: In the battles of the open she will have little to fear from the slow fumbling treacheries of the submarine,
claims.description: Submarines and torpedoes will pose little threat to surface warships in open-sea battle.

claims.quote: The struggle on the high seas between any two naval powers (except, perhaps, the English and American, who have both quite unparalleled opportunities for coaling) will not last more than a week or so.
claims.description: A naval war on the high seas will be decided within about a week.
claims.stated_time: not last more than a week or so

claims.quote: Some commerce-destroying enterprise on the part of the loser may go on, but I think the possibilities of that sort of thing are greatly exaggerated.
claims.description: Commerce raiding against merchant shipping will not be effective in future naval war.

claims.quote: The world grows smaller and smaller, the telegraph and telephone go everywhere, wireless telegraphy opens wider and wider possibilities to the imagination, and how the commerce-destroyer is to go on for long without being marked down, headed off, cut off from coal, and forced to fight or surrender, I do not see.
claims.description: Global telegraph, telephone and wireless will let navies quickly track down and sink commerce raiders.

claims.quote: And then will open a second phase of naval warfare, in which the submarine may play a larger part.
claims.description: Submarines may become important in a later phase of naval war, against coasts and ports.
